title: spilanthes langbianensis
intro: Spilanthes langbianensis, commonly known as the 'Burma Toothache Plant', is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. This plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine, particularly in Southeast Asia, for its numerous health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antimicrobial properties, which help to alleviate pain, reduce swelling, and treat infections. The therapeutic actions of Spilanthes langbianensis are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, that exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory activities. The plant's bioactive compounds have shown potential in the treatment of various health conditions, including oral infections, wounds, and skin disorders.
